item.description: Lee Chang-dong's novelistic drama tells the story of two very different couples who meet during the filming of a documentary.

item.title: 'Clayface' is underbaked body horror
item.description: Like its protagonist, the film shoots out its goopy, mud-brown, protoplasmic feelers into the undiscovered territory of horror, but it does so too tentatively.

item.title: Betty Gilpin seeks out 'anti-algorithm' projects, like 'The Lowdown' and 'Widow's Bay'
item.description: "There's an understandable pull in my industry to make things ... super safe, super familiar," Gilpin says. She wants to go the other way. Gilpin currently stars in the noir drama The Lowdown.

item.title: He left Chile on foot to England 28 years ago. He's almost finally home
item.description: British Adventurer Karl Bushby left Chile with the goal of walking an unbroken path back to his childhood home in England. Now, 28 years later, his Goliath Expedition is coming to a close.

item.title: This was once Edison Day. We re-visit his creepy talking doll
item.description: For years, the country celebrated Oct. 21 as "Edison Day," throwing parades for the famous inventor whose devices changed the world. His phonograph was the first device to play back a recorded human voice--and that invention led to his creepy talking doll, which is now considered one of his biggest failures.

item.title: Leon Bridges reinvents his sound with new album, 'Happiness Anytime'
item.description: Since his 2015 debut album, Leon Bridges has transformed himself from a Sam Cooke-style crooner into a shape-shifting singer of all things from mambo to disco. His new album is called Happiness Anytime.
